_source: Claude Opus 5, 2026-08-01. The S* catalog -- PHYSICS_SOFTWARE_MATH.md, indexed for the first time. These rows are METHODS, so they carry a SHAPE serial rather than a dimensional one: mathematics is dimensionless by construction, and forcing units onto a Kalman filter would be the same error as typing a unit nobody measured. Two rows sharing a shape serial are INTERCHANGEABLE, which is the question 'can I swap this solver' asks.

S1.03.note: Semi-implicit (symplectic) Euler. THE INTEGRATOR SOCKET. Anything with this serial can be dropped in its place -- and the choice is not cosmetic: this project measured explicit Euler NaN-ing a walker at t=3.74 s where implicitfast held. Same socket, different stability.

S1.01.note: Newton-Euler M(q)q'' + c = tau + J^T f. Takes a configuration and the KINEMATIC TREE that relates the bodies -- the graph is not decoration, it is why XML nesting deletes a class of rigging bug in this repo's own MJCF work.

S1.02.note: Composite rigid body: the mass matrix in O(n) over the joint tree. Same INPUT socket as S1.01, different output -- one gives you the motion, the other the operator.

S3.01.note: Position-based dynamics. SHARES THE INTEGRATOR SOCKET with S1.03 and that is the whole point of PBD: it is swappable for a force integrator and trades physical fidelity for unconditional stability.

S4.01.note: Discrete element method: every grain carried explicitly. A cloud in, a cloud out -- which is why this repo's granular work could run the same shape on CPU and on GPU at 6.3 billion site-updates/sec.

S6.01.note: Smoothed-particle hydrodynamics. SAME SOCKET AS DEM (S4.01), which is the honest reading of why one codebase so often does both: the difference is the interaction kernel, not the data.

S5.01.note: Vis-viva v^2 = GM(2/r - 1/a). A rare S row with a real dimensional signature -- it is a physics law that happens to live in the simulator's table. Blocked by the same gap E9.04 found: no membrane publishes a stellar mass and an orbital distance together.

S5.02.note: Kepler's equation M = E - e sin E, solved by Newton iteration. Its serial is scalar->scalar, which is honest and unhelpful: the CONTENT is that it has no closed form, and a shape serial cannot say that. A named limit of this scheme, recorded rather than papered over.

S5.03.note: Classical orbital elements: six numbers fully specify an orbit. A state becomes a vector -- this is a CHANGE OF COORDINATES, and its inverse shares the reversed serial.

S7.01.note: The rendering equation, as this project resolves it: a cloud of emitters becomes a raster. THE RASTERISER SOCKET -- anything that turns a splat buffer into pixels sits here, which is what makes the CPU and GPU paths in ParticleEngine substitutable.

S7.02.note: Spectral light transport. Same output as S7.01 but it additionally takes a SPECTRUM -- and that extra input is precisely the difference between this project's RGB renderer and the measured-optics rendering THE_GROWTH says the game is made of. The serial shows the gap as an argument.

S10.02.note: Inverse kinematics: a pose and a target become a pose. B1's foot IK is this row -- and so is any reach, any gaze, any grip closure that is told where to end.

S10.01.note: Motion matching: a predicted trajectory searched against a database of measured clips. A11's 'the real animation brain'. The `dist` is the clip library -- it is a POPULATION, not a list, which is why the 246-adult gait dataset is the right shape of thing to feed it.

S12.02.note: Stream power incision E = K A^m S^n. Dimensional, because it is geomorphology rather than method -- and aTerrain already runs it: 500 erosion steps carved the drainage network the human walks on.

S12.01.note: Thermal weathering: move material downslope wherever the local slope exceeds the talus angle. A heightfield in, a heightfield out -- THE RELAXATION SOCKET, shared by every diffusive terrain operator, which is why they can be composed in any order.
